newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU forecasters see Italy missing EMU deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: EU forecasters see Italy missing EMU deficit goal.

text.p: European Commission officials are forecasting that Italy's deficit will be 3.2 percent of its Gross Domestic Product this year, short of the qualification for the single currency, a European Union source said on Friday.

The source said the figure could change before the Commission releases its spring forecasts next Wednesday. It had been calculated by officials "at a technical level" and had now been passed higher up the Commission's political hierarchy.

EU officials and market analysts have said previously that Commission forecasters come under heavy pressure when preparing the sensitive forecasts, which indicate how close countries are coming to meeting the criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU).
For example, asked what the forecast for Germany's deficit to GDP would be, the source said: "Probably just where it needs to be."
Under the Maastricht treaty, countries must trim their deficits to no more than three 3.0 percent of GDP this year to qualify for being in the first wave of a single currency on January 1, 1997.
Preliminary forecasts published by a Portuguese newspaper on April 10 showed Italy with a defict/GDP ratio of 3.8 percent and Germany at 3.2 percent.
